AMNE 101.title: Greek and Latin Roots of English
AMNE 101.description: Greek and Latin roots of English vocabulary and grammar, with an introduction to language history and Greek and Roman culture.

AMNE 151.title: Greek and Roman Mythology
AMNE 151.description: Greek and Roman mythology and its interpretation. Emphasis on ancient texts read in English translation.

AMNE 160.title: Introduction to Religions: Judaism, Christianity, Islam
AMNE 160.description: An overview of the foundational texts, histories, and contemporary expressions of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Key concepts and approaches used in the study of religion.

AMNE 170.title: Temples, Tombs, and Tyrants: The Archaeology of the Middle East, Greece, and Rome
AMNE 170.description: The rise of civilizations, cultural interconnections, and power dynamics in the ancient Middle East (including Egypt), Greece, and Rome (10,000 BCE - 300 CE). Archaeological methods and interpretation, and analysis of ancient artifacts in UBC collections.

AMNE 200.title: Approaching the Ancient Mediterranean & Near East
AMNE 200.description: Orientation to the peoples, places, and traditions of the ancient Mediterranean and Near East, and to analyzing different forms of source material (historical, literary, archaeological) from different perspectives.

AMNE 215.title: Ancient Greece
AMNE 215.description: A survey of the ancient Greek world from the Minoan and Mycenaean (about 2000-1000 BCE) to the Hellenistic Period (323-30 BCE).

AMNE 216.title: Ancient Rome
AMNE 216.description: A survey of the ancient Roman world from the foundation of the city to the death of Constantine.

AMNE 225.title: Gladiators, Games, and Spectacle in the Greek and Roman World
AMNE 225.description: History, development, and social function of various forms of spectacle in ancient Greece and Rome, from the Olympic games to the Roman arena.

AMNE 235.title: Greek Philosophy I
AMNE 235.description: The Pre-Socratics; Socrates; Sophists; Plato. Recommended as preparation for AMNE_V 236/PHIL_V 212 and PHIL_V 310.

AMNE 236.title: Greek Philosophy II
AMNE 236.description: Aristotle; selections from Hellenistic and Late Antique Philosophy. Recommended as preparation for PHIL_V 310 and PHIL_V 311.

AMNE 251.title: Near Eastern and Biblical Mythology
AMNE 251.description: An introduction to the world of Near Eastern mythology, from the Gilgamesh Epic to the Book of Genesis and beyond.

AMNE 260.title: Scriptures of the Near East
AMNE 260.description: An introduction to the scriptures of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

AMNE 261.title: Eden to Exile: Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
AMNE 261.description: An overview of the Hebrew Bible (Old Testament), with emphasis on its ancient Near Eastern context; its competing religious perspectives; and its limits as a historical source.

AMNE 262.title: Introduction to Judaism and its Texts
AMNE 262.description: What is Judaism? An overview of the key texts that have defined the Jewish religion, from the Hebrew Bible through works of contemporary thinkers. Recommended as a basis for upper-level courses in religious studies.

AMNE 264.title: The New Testament and Early Christianity
AMNE 264.description: The origins of Christianity as reflected in the New Testament and contemporaneous literature.

AMNE 265.title: History of Christianity to 800 CE
AMNE 265.description: An introduction to the history of Christianity from its origins with Jesus through the coronation of Charlemagne as Roman Emperor in 800 CE.

AMNE 278.title: The Archaeology of Life and Death in the Roman Empire
AMNE 278.description: The lives of non-elite individuals and groups living under the Roman Empire, seen through material evidence and its interpretation. Identity, urbanism, economy, agriculture, diet, religion, Romanization, and burial. CNRS_V 104, AMNE_V 170 or ARCL_V 203 recommended as preparation.

AMNE 279.title: Byzantium: Arts of an Empire
AMNE 279.description: Art, architecture, and material culture of the Byzantine Empire situated in the eastern Mediterranean (c. 300-1453); focus on social and cultural contexts of artistic production, including interactions with neighboring cultures.

AMNE 300.title: Uses and Abuses of Antiquity
AMNE 300.description: Modern receptions and engagements with literature, history, philosophy, religion, archaeology, and art of the ancient Mediterranean and Near East with a focus on public writing.

AMNE 301.title: The Technical Terms of Medicine and Biological Science
AMNE 301.description: Acquaints the student with the Greek and Latin elements from which most specialized terms of modern medicine are constructed. Intended primarily for students planning to enter the medical, pharmaceutical, or biological sciences.

AMNE 306.title: Ancient Technology: Greece and Rome
AMNE 306.description: The origins, achievements, and social impacts of applied technology in the Greek and Roman world from the Bronze Age to Late Antiquity (c. 1500 BCE - 400 CE), with special attention to archaeological evidence.

AMNE 311.title: Prehistoric Egypt
AMNE 311.description: A survey of the development and evolution of prehistoric humans and their material culture in Egypt from the Lower Paleolithic to the Chalcolithic.

AMNE 312.title: History of Ancient Egypt
AMNE 312.description: History and culture of Ancient Egyptian civilization from political, intellectual, social and environmental perspectives.

AMNE 314.title: Early Empires of the Ancient Middle East
AMNE 314.description: A history from 3100-333 BC with emphasis on Mesopotamia.

AMNE 316.title: The Athenians and their Empire
AMNE 316.description: The sources (literary, epigraphical and other) for Athens' emergence as one of the two leading city-states in late archaic and classical Greece and the stages by which her empire grew.

AMNE 317.title: Alexander the Great and his Empire
AMNE 317.description: The rise of Macedon under Philip II leading to its domination of Greece and the overthrow of the Persian Empire by his son, Alexander; the subsequent spread of Greek civilization in the East.

AMNE 318.title: The Roman Republic
AMNE 318.description: Rome from the foundation to the Augustan settlement. Constitutional development; the workings and failure of the Republican political system; acquisition and growth of Empire; the political, social, and economic consequences of imperialism.

AMNE 319.title: The Early Roman Empire
AMNE 319.description: Roman imperial history during the Julio-Claudian and Flavian periods (30 BC-96 AD).

AMNE 320.title: Topics in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern History and Culture
AMNE 320.description: Selected topics in the history and culture of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt.

AMNE 323.title: Slavery in the Ancient Greek and Roman World
AMNE 323.description: The study and history of slavery in the Greek and Roman worlds as a political, legal, economic, social, and cultural phenomenon.

AMNE 324.title: Women in the Bronze Age, Classical Greek and Hellenistic Cultures
AMNE 324.description: The images projected in mythology, literature, and art are compared with realities of women's lives insofar as they can be reconstructed from historical, legal, and archaeological records.

AMNE 325.title: Women in the Roman World of Republican and Imperial Times
AMNE 325.description: Women in the Roman world in the culture of the Republic and the Empire. Literary, artistic, and mythological sources are compared and contrasted to historical, legal, and archaeological records.

AMNE 326.title: Ancient Greek Warfare
AMNE 326.description: Ancient Greek methods and tactics of war plus underlying social, religious and philosophical concepts relating to warfare, through sources in translation.

AMNE 327.title: The Roman Army
AMNE 327.description: Rome's military from the early Republic to the Imperial period. Topics range from those of a military nature such as equipment and strategy to social topics such as policing and marriage of soldiers.

AMNE 328.title: UnRoman Romans
AMNE 328.description: Outsider and marginalized groups in the Roman world. Topics could include representations of entertainers, immigrants, magic workers and so forth, using ancient evidence from literature to art. Restricted to students with second-year standing or above.

AMNE 331.title: Jewish Law
AMNE 331.description: History, sources, theoretical issues and current state of research about early Jewish legal traditions, focusing on close readings of classic primary texts in English translations.

AMNE 332.title: Greek Law
AMNE 332.description: The study of Greek legal theory, practice, and institutions from their origin in self-help, through the early lawgivers and their codes, to the developed system of Athens in the fifth and fourth centuries. A variety of test cases from the works of the Greek orators will be explored.

AMNE 333.title: Roman Law
AMNE 333.description: The development of Roman private law during the classical period with special attention to family law, contract and delict.

AMNE 340.title: Topics in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern Literature and Ideas
AMNE 340.description: Selected topics in the literature, ideas, and arts of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt.

AMNE 341.title: Sex, Lies, and Violence in the Hebrew Bible
AMNE 341.description: An exploration of the Bible's dark side, with emphasis on texts that center on sex, deceit, and murder.

AMNE 342.title: Translating the Bible
AMNE 342.description: Key issues involved in translating the Bible, with attention to gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, religion, and colonialism.

AMNE 345.title: Greek Epic
AMNE 345.description: Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, in translation.

AMNE 346.title: Latin Epic
AMNE 346.description: The development of the epic genre in Latin, with detailed study of Vergil's Aeneid, Ovid's Metamorphoses, and Lucan's Civil War, in translation.

AMNE 347.title: Classical Comedy
AMNE 347.description: The plays of the Greek and Roman comic dramatists: Aristophanes, Menander, Plautus and Terence, in translation.

AMNE 348.title: Classical Tragedy
AMNE 348.description: The plays of the Greek and Roman tragic dramatists, in translation. Recommended pre-requisite: One of CLST_V 105, AMNE_V 151. Restricted to students with second year standing or higher.

AMNE 351.title: Religion in Ancient Egypt
AMNE 351.description: A survey of the religious beliefs, cults, and religious institutions in Pharaonic Egypt.

AMNE 355.title: Greek Religion
AMNE 355.description: A survey of both traditional and exoteric religious practices from the Archaic to the Hellenistic period. Some knowledge of ancient Greece is recommended.

AMNE 356.title: Roman Religion
AMNE 356.description: Roman religions between the ninth century BCE and the fourth century CE, including mystery religions, magic, emperor worship, and early Christianity, with particular attention devoted to the primary sources. Some knowledge of ancient Rome is recommended.

AMNE 360.title: Topics in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern Religion
AMNE 360.description: Selected topics on the religions of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt.

AMNE 361.title: The Origins of Judaism
AMNE 361.description: Surveys the history of Jews and Judaism in the Second Temple era, from the destruction of the First Jerusalem Temple (586 B.C.E.) to the beginnings of the rabbinic movement (200 C.E.).

AMNE 363.title: Talmud, Midrash and the Rabbinic Imagination
AMNE 363.description: The Talmud, Midrash, and other late-antique (3rd - 7th centuries) rabbinic writings, focusing on biblical interpretation and narratives.

AMNE 364.title: Magic, Prophecy, and Divination in the Biblical World
AMNE 364.description: Textual, contextual, and comparative exploration of the reciprocal relations between gods and people in the Hebrew Bible, Near Eastern ritual texts, and ancient experience.

AMNE 366.title: The Origins of Christianity
AMNE 366.description: The origins of Christianity as reflected in early Christian literature of the first and early second centuries (including the New Testament).

AMNE 368.title: Paul and the Making of Christianity
AMNE 368.description: Study of the controversial figure of Paul of Tarsus: his writings, impact, and reception, with attention to the contexts of ancient Judaism and the Roman Empire. AMNE_V 264 or previous experience reading the New Testament is recommended.

AMNE 369.title: Jesus: Between History and Literature
AMNE 369.description: The figure of Jesus, his teachings, and his reception through literary and contextual analysis of the canonical and apocryphal gospels.
notes: Recommended: AMNE_V 264 or previous experience reading the New Testament

AMNE 370.title: Topics in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern Archaeology
AMNE 370.description: Selected topics on the art, archaeology and/or architecture of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt.

AMNE 371.title: Ancient Egypt: The Archaeology of the Land of the Pharaohs
AMNE 371.description: The material remains of the ancient Egyptians from monumental tombs and temples to the artifacts of daily life; the development of Egyptian civilization from the rise of the first rulers to its incorporation into the Roman Empire.

AMNE 372.title: The Archaeology of Ancient Iraq and Syria: Babylon and Beyond
AMNE 372.description: An overview of the archaeology of the ancient Near East, with special emphasis on the civilizations of Mesopotamia, from the appearance of the first cities (c. 3400 BCE) to the end of the Persian period (c. 330 BCE). AMNE_V 170 recommended as preparation.

AMNE 373.title: Archaeology and the Bible
AMNE 373.description: The impact of archaeological research on understanding the history and religion of ancient Israel.

AMNE 376.title: Greek Art and Architecture
AMNE 376.description: The visual culture of the ancient Greek world in the second and first millennia BCE, especially from c. 1000 to 30 BCE.

AMNE 377.title: Roman Art and Architecture
AMNE 377.description: The visual culture of the ancient Roman world from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE.

AMNE 379.title: Art and the Religious Transformation of the Late Roman Empire
AMNE 379.description: Visual culture and religious diversity of the Late Roman Empire (2nd-7th c.); social, political, and religious contexts of art, including diverse viewing practices and cultural frameworks.

AMNE 381.title: Theories of Myth
AMNE 381.description: Origins, nature, and transmission of myth in the Western tradition, with particular attention devoted to the interpretation of myth from ancient times up to the present. Some background in myth is recommended.

AMNE 382.title: Egyptomania
AMNE 382.description: The adaptation and appropriation of ancient Egypt in ancient and modern art, architecture, film, and music; the development of Egyptology since the 19th century.

AMNE 383.title: Modern Jewish Ethics in Historical Perspective
AMNE 383.description: Readings from key texts in English translation, tracing how Jewish approaches to ethical issues evolved from biblical times to the present.

AMNE 384.title: Reading the Bible on Indigenous Lands
AMNE 384.description: Reception, use, and appropriation of biblical texts to support European settler colonialism on Turtle Island (North America), with a focus on British Columbia. Impacts of Christianity on Indigenous communities, including the Indian Act and Residential School system.

AMNE 391.title: Introduction to Middle Egyptian
AMNE 391.description: Language of Ancient Egypt and the main literary texts composed during the Middle Kingdom.

AMNE 392.title: Introduction to Akkadian
AMNE 392.description: The basic grammar and introduction to the cuneiform writing system of the Akkadian language of the Ancient Near East.

AMNE 393.title: Introduction to Coptic
AMNE 393.description: An introduction to Coptic, the language of Christian Egypt from 100 AD.

AMNE 394.title: Introduction to Aramaic
AMNE 394.description: Basics of Imperial Aramaic grammar and vocabulary, with readings from biblical and other ancient sources from the eastern Mediterranean and Southwest and Central Asia.

AMNE 395.title: Practicum in Ancient Mediterranean or Near Eastern Archaeology
AMNE 395.description: Training in excavation techniques and interpretation through participation in the excavation of a Greek, Roman, or Near Eastern site in Europe or the Middle East. The minimum length of the course is three weeks; it may be repeated once. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 395 and CNRS_V 335. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 396.title: Experiencing the Ancient World Abroad
AMNE 396.description: International field experience and study of ancient Mediterranean or Near Eastern sites and materials held in museums. Topics and locations may vary. Consult Department for current offerings.

AMNE 420.title: Seminar in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern History and Culture
AMNE 420.description: Selected topics in the history and culture of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt, with an emphasis on research. A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 420 and CLST_V 401. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 440.title: Seminar in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern Literature and Ideas
AMNE 440.description: Selected topics in the literature, ideas, and arts of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt, with an emphasis on research. A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 440 and CLST_V 402. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 441.title: Literature of Ancient Egypt or the Ancient Near East
AMNE 441.description: Topics in the main genres and texts of Egyptian and/or Ancient Near Eastern Literature and their modern interpretation. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 441, NEST_V 401, NEST_V 505, and AMNE_V 541. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 461.title: Seminar in Biblical Studies
AMNE 461.description: Selected topics in biblical and related texts. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 461 or RELG_V 475. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 462.title: Seminar in Early Judaism
AMNE 462.description: Selected topics in Judaism and Hellenism, the rise of the synagogue, Jewish sects, the development of classical rabbinic literature (e.g., Mishnah, Talmud, Midrash). A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 462 or RELG_V 407. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 470.title: Seminar in Ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern Archaeology
AMNE 470.description: Selected topics in the art, archaeology and/or architecture of the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt, with an emphasis on research. A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 470 and CLST_V 403. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 471.title: The Archaeology of Urbanism
AMNE 471.description: Selected topics on the origins, development, and material manifestations of urbanism in the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 471, NEST_V 402, AMNE_V 571 and NEST_V 506. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 472.title: The Archaeology of Ancient Cyprus
AMNE 472.description: An overview of the archaeology of ancient Cyprus from the island's initial colonization in the 10th millennium BCE through the period of its rule as part of the Roman Empire (4th century CE).

AMNE 480.title: Seminar in the Reception of the Ancient Mediterranean and Near East
AMNE 480.description: Selected topics in the reception of the ancient Mediterranean, Near Eastern and/or Egyptian cultures from their own times to the present, with an emphasis on research. A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 480 and CLST_V 404. Students should consult the AMNE Undergraduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 500.title: Pro-Seminar in Ancient Mediterranean Studies: Selected Topics
AMNE 500.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 500 or CNRS_V 500. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 501.title: Topics in Egyptology
AMNE 501.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 501 or NEST_ 503. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 525.title: Topics in Greek History and Culture
AMNE 525.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 525 or GREK_V 535.

AMNE 527.title: Topics in Roman History and Culture
AMNE 527.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 527 or LATN_V 535.

AMNE 530.title: Topics in Law and Society
AMNE 530.description: A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 530 or CNRS_V 502. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 540.title: Topics in Literature, Art and Society
AMNE 540.description: A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 540 or CNRS_V 503. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 541.title: Literature of Ancient Egypt or the Ancient Near East
AMNE 541.description: Topics in the main genres and texts of Egyptian and/or Ancient Near Eastern Literature and their modern interpretation. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 541, NEST_V 505, AMNE_V 441 or NEST_V 401. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 560.title: Topics in Religion
AMNE 560.description: A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 560 or CNRS_V 504. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 561.title: Topics in Biblical Studies
AMNE 561.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 561 or RELG_V 500. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 562.title: Topics in Early Judaism
AMNE 562.description: Studies in the texts (in translation), history, and religious thought of Judaism after the close of the Biblical Period. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 562 or RELG_V 502. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 563.title: Topics in Early Christianity
AMNE 563.description: Selected topics pertaining to the literature, history, and material culture of Christians from the first century CE through late antiquity. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 563 or RELG_V 503. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 571.title: The Archaeology of Urbanism
AMNE 571.description: Selected topics on the origins, development, and material manifestations of urbanism in the ancient Mediterranean, Near East and/or Egypt. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 571, NEST_V 506, AMNE_V 471 or NEST_V 402. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 572.title: Topics in Near Eastern Archaeology
AMNE 572.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 572 or NEST_V 500. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 575.title: Topics in Greek Archaeology
AMNE 575.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 575 or CLST_V 518. Students should consult with the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 576.title: Topics in Greek Regional Archaeology
AMNE 576.description: Study of a particular area, e.g., Ionia, Sicily, Southern Italy. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 576 or CLST_V 511. Students should consult with the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 577.title: Topics in Roman Archaeology
AMNE 577.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 577 or CLST_V 519. Students should consult with the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 578.title: Topics in Roman Provincial Archaeology
AMNE 578.description: Study of a particular area, e.g., Gaul, Britain, Asia Minor. A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 578 or CLST_V 512. Students should consult with the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 581.title: Theory and Method in the Study of Religion

AMNE 590.title: Topics in Identity
AMNE 590.description: A maximum of 12 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 590 or CNRS_V 505. Students should consult the AMNE Graduate Advisor before registering.

AMNE 591.title: Ancient Mediterranean or Near Eastern Language Studies
AMNE 591.description: A maximum of 6 credits will be granted for AMNE_V 591 or LATN_V 540.

AMNE 595.title: Practicum in Ancient Mediterranean or Near Eastern Archaeology
AMNE 595.description: Training in excavation techniques and interpretation through participation in the excavation of a Greek, Roman, or Near Eastern site in Europe or the Middle East. The minimum length of the course is three weeks.
